findings.text: H5003 (na'aph, 15 verses): the meaning block gives the literal sense first (to commit adultery, always with the wife of another), but its verses are dominated by Israel's idolatry: Hos 3:1 (love a woman as the Lord loves the children of Israel, though they turn to other gods), Jer 3:9 (committing adultery with stone and tree), Ezek 23:37 and 45 (the extended two-sisters allegory). Only the Decalogue citation (Exod 20:14, with Deut 5:18) and a couple of narrative uses are literal without a second layer.

findings.text: G3429 and G3431 (moichaō, moicheuō, 15 verses combined) carry the clearest literal-teaching strand of the family: Jesus' divorce and remarriage teaching (Matt 5:32, 19:9, Mark 10:11) and the repeated Decalogue citations across the Synoptics and Epistles (Matt 19:18, Mark 10:19, Luke 18:20, Rom 13:9, Jas 2:11).
Even in the literal-teaching strand, G3431's meaning block notes that the same word covers spiritual adultery, being guilty of idolatry (Rev 2:22).

G4205 (pornos, 10 verses) functions almost entirely as a vice-list category, who is excluded from the kingdom, paired consistently with idolaters as a fixed collocation (1 Cor 5:10-11, 6:9, Eph 5:5, Rev 21:8, 22:15), reinforcing the same adultery and idolatry pairing from a different angle.
